thread:
sara: Hey team — BrightBeam hit a burst of 429s and p95 token latency spiking in their dedicated eu-west-1 pool. Reported right after an autoscale event. stack: text-generation, model=gpt-open-8b. Tenant id bb-4812. Can someone take a look?

mike: On it. Do you have exact times and any API error snippets?

sara: Root: 2025-11-02T14:33:10Z, repeated 429s and some 503s. Example response: 
`{"error":"rate_limited","detail":"request throttled: tenant_rate_limit"}`
Also saw p95 token latency jump from ~120ms -> 1.2s for a ~3m window.

ashley: Can you paste the node assignment / MIG partition details for the requests? My suspicion is noisy-neighbor on MIG sibling (SM/bandwidth saturation). What's the sequence length distribution?

sara: Seq len median ~128, 95th ~512 (lots of long chats). Node/slot from logs: node-ml-45, slot: mig-1g. Command I ran: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." https://api.redwood/tenant/bb-4812/slots` — coming back mig-1g on node-ml-45 repeatedly.

kevin: FYI I pulled node-ml-45 metrics: SM util on GPU0 95% for several minutes, GPU memory 90%. sibling slice (gpu1) had very low SM util but high memory bandwidth. Looks like KV cache thrash + memory bandwidth saturation.

autoscale-bot: Autoscale event: pool eu-west-1-dedicated increased from 2 -> 4 nodes at 2025-11-02T14:31:40Z due to CPU-based policy. New nodes have mixed partitioning: 2x full-GPU, 2x mixed MIG (1g+2g).

mike: That mix can cause placement anomalies — BrightBeam was scheduled onto a MIG 1g on node-ml-45 which shared host with a noisy tenant running long-context inference loops. We see throttles triggered by per-tenant token rate guard and backend overload heuristics.

sara: Is moving them to a different slot safe without downtime? Customer reporting degraded UX.

kevin: Short-term: we can migrate their active slot to an idle full-GPU slot on a different node via `rctl migrate --tenant bb-4812 --target node-ml-47:gpu0`. It requires a soft drain (brief reconnect). Medium-term: enforce homogeneous partitioning for that pool or change autoscale policy to create identical node types.

ashley: Repro steps I did locally: replicated long tails by running concurrent long-sequence chat sessions on sibling slice. Observed KV cache eviction spikes and L3/DRAM bandwidth thrash. Dump of `nvidia-smi topo -v` and `perf` counters attached in the support ticket (linked).

mike: Action items: 
1) kevin — schedule migration for bb-4812 to node-ml-47 (slot gpu0) now (ETA 5m)
2) sara — open CS check-in and propose a credit for the impacted window
3) infra follow-up: change autoscale profile to prefer homogeneous node templates for eu-west-1-dedicated and add a placement rule to avoid mixing MIG+full types in same pool

sara: I'll call the customer after migration. Can we also add a short-term firewall on the noisy tenant if it keeps thrashing?

kevin: We can throttle that tenant via placement QoS and set an emergency rate cap if it exceeds X tokens/s. I'll add a temporary cap and monitor.

ashley: Logged a memo to eng-ml about improving KV cache awareness in the scheduler (so long contexts don't evict neighbor caches). We'll prioritize after triage.

sara: Thanks all — please add any follow-up notes to the ticket. I'll update BrightBeam once migration completes. :thumbsup:
